cohort: 428 mothers at a Tertiary University Hospital in Greece who were interviewed after at least 24 hours from childbirth
finding: Maternal BMI and immigrant status, information provided by midwives and encouragement, rooming-in and mode of childbirth (caesarean section), were found to be important for breast-feeding initiation in this study population.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was negatively associated with both exclusive breastfeeding initiation and any breastfeeding initiation.
